detail.title: Islamic Blended Finance for Circular Economy Impactful SMEs To Achieve SDGs

publicationDetails.detailsText: The Singapore Economic Review, volume 67, issue 01, 2022[10.1142/S0217590820420060]

detail.abstract: In this research, we present a framework for blended Islamic finance for impactful small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to achieve sustainable development goals (SDGs). The blend results from discussing the pertinent perspectives that underlie the motives of philanthropy, private sector activities, and public sector facilitation. The consensus of these three stakeholders on the impact criteria is an essential precondition for the blend to happen. Therefore, we first developed the consensus-based impact criteria for SMEs, namely, 4Zeros & SS (zero-waste, zero-emissions, zero-interest, Zero foreclosures and service to society). After that, we adopted a financial engineering approach to design products by blending the three motives. Financial contracts could be incentive compatible and effective if these three motivations are recognized and brought together. The purpose of our research is to offer such incentive-compatible structures that can mobilize funding for impactful SMEs, save cost as well as generate revenue for self-sustainability. In the contract design, the private sector provides finance, the philanthropist pays the costs of funds, the public sector facilitates, and the impactful SME gets subsidized financing. Since the blended nature of the contract provides a social subsidy to fund the cost element of the financing, the proposed structure creates a win-win result for the blending parties. While financial institutions expand into the SMEs sector for profitability, blended Islamic finance will attract additional resources toward enhancing development impact. Through the philanthropic component, SMEs, on the other hand, will access the source of social subsidy that will relieve the burden of the exorbitant commercial rates. The funding structure will reduce risk perception and spur growth. Consequently, this collaborative and innovative contract design will contribute to achieving multidimensional human development, as enshrined in the Maqasid al-Shariah, and the SDGs. Impactful businesses must integrate environmental, social and governance best practices as well as national development goals. Hence, the proposal offers several benefits and prospects of extended use for other consensus-based purposes such as low-cost housing, solar paneling, health, education, etc.

title: Digital Justice in Health Access: Algorithmic Governance in Kenya's Maternal Health Informatics

detail.title: Digital Justice in Health Access: Algorithmic Governance in Kenya's Maternal Health Informatics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

keywords: Linda Jamii Science and Technology Studies

detail.abstract: This research conducts a comparative conceptual framework analysis (CCFA) of Linda Mama and Linda Jamii, two prominent maternal health initiatives in Kenya that illustrate divergent digital logics of care: the welfare-state model and the market-driven model. Both projects utilise digital infrastructures, biometric registration, mobile platforms, and algorithmic management to improve healthcare accessibility. Nevertheless, they represent divergent moral and political ideologies regarding the criteria for deserving care, the implementation of dignity, and the recognition of various types of citizenship in the digital realm. Utilising Amartya Sen's Capability Approach, Nancy Fraser's theory of justice, and digital ethics frameworks, the study examines how each program defines justice, dignity, and inclusiveness in the context of digital governance. The analysis used CCFA to systematically deconstruct and compare the conceptual architectures of both frameworks through the examination of publicly accessible governmental documents, academic literature, and evaluation reviews. It examines how Linda Mama digitises the maternal body as a locus of public entitlement and surveillance, whereas Linda Jamii transforms poverty into data through market-driven micro-insurance frameworks, reconceptualising women as consumers of risk instead of citizens with rights. This comparative perspective uncovers the ethical contradictions of digitised dignity, illustrating how digital inclusion fosters visibility while exacerbating vulnerability. The article contends that both programs, notwithstanding their digital potential, may exacerbate structural imbalances if ethical and participative protections are not integrated into their design. It ends by asking for a digital health framework that puts justice at the centre and is based on African communitarian philosophies of care like Ubuntu, as well as on consent, data ethics, and inclusivity. By contrasting state and market paradigms of digital maternal care, the study enhances ongoing discussions regarding digital justice, algorithmic governance, and the moral economy of public health in the Global South.

title: Operational Excellence through Lean Manufacturing and Certification Standards
affiliations: Supply Chain Executive

detail.title: Operational Excellence through Lean Manufacturing and Certification Standards
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the intersection of Lean manufacturing methodologies and global certification standards in achieving operational excellence. It reviews Lean principles, Six Sigma practices, and the integration of Lean Six Sigma as drivers of process efficiency and defect reduction. In parallel, it examines how standards such as ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, and ethical compliance frameworks like SMETA institutionalize quality, sustainability, and safety. Empirical evidence and case studies show that organizations that integrate Lean initiatives with certification systems achieve superior performance in productivity, quality, and market competitiveness. The paper argues that operational excellence is best realized through this dual approach: Lean methodologies provide continuous improvement momentum, while certification standards provide structure, credibility, and long-term sustainability.

title: Fortifying Global Supply Chains: Practical Insights on Risk Management and Operational Continuity
affiliations: Supply Chain Executive

detail.title: Fortifying Global Supply Chains: Practical Insights on Risk Management and Operational Continuity
detail.abstract: Global supply chains face unprecedented risks from pandemics, geopolitical events, cyber threats, and natural disasters. This paper explores strategies for building resilience and ensuring operational continuity in manufacturing supply chains. Drawing on both scholarly research and the author's leadership experience at Amazon, Givi Vietnam, Coepto, and QPack Far East, the discussion highlights the balance between Lean efficiency and resilience, proactive risk identification, cross-functional coordination, and the integration of predictive analytics and Industry 4.0 technologies. Case studies including Amazon's COVID-19 response and Givi Vietnam's quarantine strategy, illustrate how supplier diversification, contingency planning, and collaborative leadership sustain performance in crises. The paper concludes that effective risk management is not only defensive but also a source of competitive advantage.

title: Regulating Social Media: The Fight Over Section 230 — and Beyond
affiliations: New York University (NYU) - New York University

detail.title: Regulating Social Media: The Fight Over Section 230 — and Beyond

keywords: and chief privacy officer at Microsoft
visiting fellow at Cornell Tech's Digital Life Initiative

detail.abstract:
Recently, Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act of 1996 has come under sharp attack from members of both political parties, including presidential candidates Donald Trump and Joe Biden. The foundational law of the commercial internet, Section 230 does two things: It protects platforms and websites from most lawsuits related to content posted by third parties. And it guarantees this shield from liability even if the platforms and sites actively police the content they host. This protection has encouraged internet companies to innovate and grow, even as it has raised serious questions about whether social media platforms adequately self-regulate harmful content.

In addition to the assaults by Trump and Biden, members of Congress have introduced a number of bills designed to limit the reach of Section 230. Some critics have asserted unrealistically that repealing or curbing Section 230 would solve a wide range of problems relating to internet governance. These critics also have played down the potentially dire consequences that repeal would have for smaller internet companies. Academics, think tank researchers, and others outside of government have made a variety of more nuanced proposals for revising the law. We assess these ideas with an eye toward recommending and integrating the most promising ones. Our conclusion is that Section 230 ought to be preserved—but that it can be improved. It should be used as a means to push platforms to accept greater responsibility for the content they host.

There are ways of improving governance of social media platforms that go beyond revising Section 230. One promising idea is to create a specialized government agency to improve transparency and accountability without interfering in particular content decisions. Facebook has suggested that a government body could monitor the “prevalence” of harmful content on various platforms, set benchmarks for such content, and impose sanctions for failure to meet the benchmarks. To pass constitutional muster, such plans would have to steer clear of the First Amendment’s prohibition of government action “abridging the freedom of speech.” We also analyze these ideas in the pages that follow.

title: Tackling Domestic Disinformation: What the Social Media Companies Need to Do
affiliations: New York University (NYU) - New York University

detail.title: Tackling Domestic Disinformation: What the Social Media Companies Need to Do
detail.abstract:
A growing amount of misleading and false content infests social media. A 2018 study by researchers at Oxford University found that 25 percent of Facebook and Twitter shares related to the midterm elections in the U.S. contained “junk news”—deliberately deceptive or incorrect information. A majority of this harmful content came not from Russia or other foreign state actors but from domestic U.S. sources. 

This report focuses on domestically generated disinformation in the U.S.: the nature and scope of the problem, what the social media platforms have done about it, and what more they need to do. Domestic disinformation comes from disparate sources, including message boards, websites, and networks of accounts on Facebook, Twitter, and YouTube. This homegrown harmful content flows from both liberals and conservatives, but overall, it is predominantly a right-wing phenomenon. Social media researchers have said that highly partisan conservatives are more likely than highly partisan liberals to encounter and share disinformation. 

Increasingly, social media platforms are removing disinformation from Russia and other foreign countries because of its fraudulent nature and potential to disrupt democratic institutions. In contrast, some commentators have argued that misleading content produced by U.S. citizens is difficult to distinguish from ordinary political communication protected by the First Amendment. According to this view, we shouldn’t encourage the platforms to make judgments about what’s true and untrue in politics. 

But the platforms are already making similar judgments when their algorithms rank and recommend posts, tweets, and videos. They also remove certain categories of harmful content, such as harassment and hate speech. We urge them to add provably false information to the removal list, starting with content affecting politics or democratic institutions. The First Amendment, which precludes government censorship, doesn’t constrict social media venues owned and operated by nongovernmental entities. The real question confronting the platforms is how to make their evaluations of factually questionable content more reasonably, consistently, and transparently.

title: A Platform ‘Weaponized’: How YouTube Spreads Harmful Content – And What Can Be Done About It
affiliations: New York University (NYU) - New York University and New York University (NYU) - New York University

detail.title: A Platform ‘Weaponized’: How YouTube Spreads Harmful Content – And What Can Be Done About It
detail.abstract:
YouTube, the most popular social media platform in the United States, dominates user-generated long-form video-sharing around the world. Like other major platforms, it has a dual nature: It provides two billion users access to news, entertainment, and do-it-yourself videos, but it also serves as a venue for political disinformation, public health myths, and incitement of violence. 

YouTube’s role in Russia illustrates this duality. Since Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, YouTube has offered ordinary Russians factual information about the war, even as the Kremlin has blocked or restricted other Western-based social media platforms and pressured foreign journalists in the country to silence themselves. But for years before the brutal incursion, YouTube served as a megaphone for Vladimir Putin’s disinformation about Ukraine and its relations with the West.

Despite its heft and influence, less is known about YouTube than other major social media sites. A subsidiary of Google, YouTube has been less scrutinized by social scientists, politicians, and civil society groups, including ours. As a result, we know less about YouTube’s business practices and the effects they have on the societies in which it operates. This report seeks to address this knowledge deficit.

In Part 2, we examine YouTube’s role as the internet’s vast video library, one which has contributed to the spread of misinformation and other harmful content. In 2019, for example, YouTube reacted to complaints that its recommendations were pushing impressionable users toward extremist right-wing views. The company made a series of changes to its algorithms, resulting in a decline in recommendations of conspiratorial and false content.

But recommendations are not the only way that people find videos on YouTube. A troubling amount of extremist content remains available for users who search for it. Moreover, YouTube’s extensive program for sharing advertising revenue with popular creators means that purveyors of misinformation can make a living while amplifying the grievances and resentments that foment partisan hatred, particularly on the political right.

title: AI-assisted Programming May Decrease the Productivity of Experienced Developers by Increasing Maintenance Burden
affiliations: , Tilburg University, Tilburg University,  and Tilburg University - Tilburg University School of Economics and Management

detail.title: AI-assisted Programming May Decrease the Productivity of Experienced Developers by Increasing Maintenance Burden
detail.abstract: Generative AI solutions like GitHub Copilot have been shown to increase the productivity of software developers. Yet prior work remains unclear on the quality of code produced and the challenges of maintaining it in software projects. If quality declines as volume grows, experienced developers face increased workloads reviewing and reworking code from less-experienced contributors. We analyze developer activity in Open Source Software (OSS) projects following the introduction of GitHub Copilot. We find that productivity indeed increases. However, the increase in productivity is primarily driven by less-experienced (peripheral) developers. We also find that code written after the adoption of AI requires more rework. Importantly, the added rework burden falls on the more experienced (core) developers, who review 6.5% more code after Copilot's introduction, but show a 19% drop in their original code productivity. More broadly, this finding raises caution that productivity gains of AI may mask the growing burden of maintenance on a shrinking pool of experts.

title: Making ESG Real: A Return to Values-Driven Investing
affiliations: New York University (NYU) - Center for Business and Human Rights

detail.title: Making ESG Real: A Return to Values-Driven Investing
detail.abstract:
Investing based on environmental, social, and governance factors— ESG investing—faces criticism from two main sources. Conservative U.S. politicians have tried to stir ill-informed hysteria over what they deride as “woke capitalism.” Separately, a very different group of skeptics that includes academics and journalists have relied on serious research and arguments to raise questions about whether current forms of ESG investing can deliver on their promises. 

Informed by these legitimate scholarly and journalistic critiques, we offer a dramatically different approach that can revive the original goal of ESG investing—namely, using investment decisions to create incentives for companies to conduct themselves in a more responsible fashion. 

The conceptual error at the heart of current ESG frameworks is that they measure how environmental and social risks may harm shareholders, rather than how business may harm the world. We show how this misconception developed historically and unpack the three reasons that it’s misguided. First, firms often take actions that harm society without shareholders suffering consequences. Second, enlightened ESG policies often add costs that investors are unwilling to tolerate because they reduce shareholder returns, although many E policies and some S policies may be cost-justified in the long-run. Third, centering ESG on financial returns misleads many investors who assume that a fund labeled “ESG” is values-driven. Instead they are fed exaggerated marketing claims by funds that are failing to achieve the traditional objective of protecting society. 

Much of the legitimate critical literature dwells on the incoherence of current ESG ratings. Scholars agree that the scores given to the same company by different ESG raters are deeply uncorrelated. ESG funds use any number of semi-secret rating frameworks, applying different weights to countless different metrics and criteria. Some of the most crucial data—for instance, on global value chains—is chronically missing or goes unmeasured. Firms that excel in one facet of ESG may lag in another, and the component factors often work at cross-purposes, yet the frameworks typically assign companies a single composite “ESG” score. With so much noise around the ESG signal, no one can quite tell what values investors are expressing or what conduct they’re encouraging.

detail.abstract: Background: Nurse performance is crucial to quality healthcare services, yet it remains a global challenge. Objective: This systematic review examines the influence of proper leadership styles on nurse performance. Methods: A systematic review was conducted using the PRISMA guidelines. A total of 846 articles were then selected based on original articles, studies conducted on nurses, and full-text articles in English. The final seven articles were screened and included in this systematic review. Results: Paradoxical, ethical, situational, transformational, servant, and authentic leadership styles have a significant positive impact on nurse performance through mediating mechanisms such as organisational commitment, empowerment, self-compassion, innovation, and job retention. title: Fueling the Fire: How Social Media Intensifies U.S. Political Polarization – And What Can Be Done About It
affiliations: New York University (NYU) - New York University, New York University (NYU) - New York University and New York University (NYU) - New York University

detail.title: Fueling the Fire: How Social Media Intensifies U.S. Political Polarization – And What Can Be Done About It
detail.abstract:
Some critics of the social media industry contend that widespread use of Facebook, Twitter, and YouTube has contributed to increased political polarization in the United States. But Facebook, the largest social media platform, has disputed this contention, saying that it is unsupported by social science research. Determining whether social media plays a role in worsening partisan animosity is important because political polarization has pernicious consequences. 

In the U.S., where partisan divisiveness has reached new extremes, these consequences include declining trust in fellow citizens and major institutions; erosion of democratic norms like respect for elections; loss of faith in the existence of commonly held facts; and political violence such as the January 6, 2021, insurrection on Capitol Hill.

This report analyzes the evidence bearing on social media’s role in polarization, assesses the effects of severe divisiveness, and recommends steps the government and the social media industry can take to ameliorate the problem. We conclude that Facebook, Twitter, and YouTube are not the original or main cause of rising U.S. political polarization, a phenomenon that long predates the social media industry. But use of those platforms intensifies divisiveness and thus contributes to its corrosive consequences. This conclusion is bolstered by a close reading of the social science literature, interviews with sociologists and political scientists who have published studies in this area, and Facebook’s own pattern of internally researching the polarization problem and periodically adjusting its algorithms to reduce the flow of content likely to stoke political extremism and hatred.

Political polarization is a complicated concept. Democracy entails disagreement. Democrats clash with Republicans over taxes, immigration, and other issues, while demands for social justice may provoke controversy and backlash. In other words, in a democratic system, politics naturally creates some degree of polarization. But in light of the harmful consequences of the extreme divisiveness now plaguing the U.S., limiting polarization ought to be an urgent priority.

We focus on “affective polarization,” a form of partisan hostility characterized by seeing one’s opponents as not only wrong on important issues, but also abhorrent, unpatriotic, and a danger to the country’s future. This kind of hatred now infects American politics, and social media has helped spread the disease. But as we illustrate, affective polarization and its consequences are not distributed evenly across the political spectrum. Donald Trump’s presidency and his continued influence over many conservatives have helped push the right to further extremes than the left has gone. January 6 provides a vivid example.

This report presents findings from a 2025 survey of U.S. law faculty about their own use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT and how their students use them as well.  Most respondents reported using AI at least occasionally for teaching-related purposes, and many estimated that a majority of their students used it in their courses.

The report concludes with implications for policy, pedagogy, and future research.

title: Hanging Purchase And Landing Returns: An Empirical Study Of Product Returns In Pre-Sale Promotions

detail.title: Hanging Purchase And Landing Returns: An Empirical Study Of Product Returns In Pre-Sale Promotions
detail.abstract: Problem definition: With increasing competition during large-scale promotions, pre-sale promotions have emerged as an innovative tool for platforms to boost sales by extending the promotional period through a two-stage payment structure, with a deposit followed by a final payment. Compared with regular promotions requiring a single payment, we examine how this payment design affects consumer satisfaction by analyzing its causal impact on product returns. Methodology/results: Using transaction-level data from a major Chinese e-commerce platform, where sales events begin with a pre-sale promotion followed by a regular promotion, we construct matched samples and apply an instrumental variable approach to address endogeneity. We find that pre-sale promotions raise the return probability by 13.91% relative to regular promotions. This result is robust to different instruments, alternative models, and tighter matching criteria. Further analysis shows that the effect is not driven by post-purchase search or the pain of paying, but by the waiting period between payments. This "hanging purchase" heightens cognitive tension, leading consumers to scrutinize products more critically and increasing returns. Managerial implications: Understanding how and why pre-sale promotions influence product returns is essential for e-commerce platforms to mitigate risks while continuing to benefit from this two-stage payment design. To reduce returns, a direct approach is to shorten the deposit stage, thereby mitigating the adverse impact associated with the long waiting period. Offering consumers the option of automatic deduction for the final payment also represents a practical method to ease cognitive tension without undermining sales potential.

Digital twins are combined with cutting-edge technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and smart connected products, providing unparalleled personalization and efficiency in customer interaction. This review fills important research gaps by examining how digital twins can transform marketing strategies through improved consumer insights and more precise business decisions. Five themes are identified and they are 1. Digitalization and its Impact on Business and Identity, 2. The Role of Digital Platforms in Shaping Experiences, 3. Strategic Learning and Business Model Transformation, 4. Consumer Manipulation Through Advertising and Digital Technologies, and 5. Cultural Heritage and Digital Communication. The Integrated Digital Twin Marketing Process Framework was explained which is dynamic and multi-stage process. The review suggests future research, highlighting the importance of a more in-depth examination of the long-term effects of digital twins on marketing and consumer interaction. This study seeks to provide an in-depth understanding of digital twins, offering insights that could guide both academic research and practical applications in marketing.

title: Digital Development and Employment Transformation: Evidence from Regional Heterogeneity in China

detail.title: Digital Development and Employment Transformation: Evidence from Regional Heterogeneity in China
detail.abstract: Purpose-This study analyzes the dynamic impact of digital development on employment patterns in China and explores the moderating role of institutional factors, offering valuable insights for promoting sustainable employment transformation in emerging economies. Design/methodology/approach-This research constructs a comprehensive provincial digital development index. Dynamic panel System GMM models are applied to a balanced panel dataset of Chinese provinces from 2012 to 2022 to analyze heterogeneous effects across regions, sectors, and skill levels. Findings-The empirical findings reveal a complex, institutionally-contingent employment transformation. The aggregate impact is a short-term net positive, showing immediate job creation followed by a partial adjustment. This is driven by profound structural reconfiguration: a regional "threshold effect" concentrates job growth in highincome areas, employment shifts systemically to the tertiary sector, and both high-skilled (promotion-suppression) and low-skilled (displacement-rebound) labor markets face dramatic churn. Institutional conditions are critical: human capital's moderating effect is insignificant, suggesting a "skill mismatch," while government education spending has a negative moderating effect, implying a "talent crowding-out effect." Practical implications-Developing countries must adopt coordinated policies to harness digitalization: reforming education to meet market demand, using targeted regional policies to help lagging areas cross the "digital threshold," and optimizing public spending to foster synergy and avoid potential crowding-out effects. Originality/value-This study systematically examines the dynamic, non-linear, and structural employment effects of digitalization in a developing country context, integrating institutional analysis with dynamic panel models to reveal the policy-contingent digitalization-employment nexus.

title: Reducing Inequality through Dual Channels: Lowering Essential Living Costs and Raising Baseline Wealth

detail.title: Reducing Inequality through Dual Channels: Lowering Essential Living Costs and Raising Baseline Wealth
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a conceptual framework for understanding and addressing inequality through two complementary policy levers: lowering essential living costs and raising baseline wealth. Traditional approaches to inequality emphasize income redistribution, typically measured through indices such as the Gini coefficient. However, these measures often fail to capture two critical dimensions of lived economic experience: (i) the burden of essential expenditures (housing, healthcare, education, transportation), and (ii) the presence or absence of baseline wealth that prevents downward mobility and secures intergenerational opportunity. Inequality, in this framework, can be represented as a function of cost pressures and wealth floors: where C denotes an index of essential living costs and W_0 represents a baseline wealth guarantee. Reducing inequality, therefore, requires a dual strategy: decreasing cost burdens and increasing baseline wealth. This approach offers three contributions. First, it extends the measurement of inequality beyond income distribution by explicitly incorporating cost-of-living and wealth floors. Second, it provides policymakers with two clear levers that can be evaluated and quantified. Third, it highlights the potential for new indices that adjust or complement the Gini coefficient to better reflect the real conditions of inequality across societies. This framework opens avenues for empirical testing, cross-national comparison, and the design of policy innovations such as "essential cost indices" and "baseline wealth accounts.

detail.abstract: Over the past two years, I've become somewhat obsessed with understanding how Myanmar language navigates our increasingly English-dominated digital world. As someone who's never actually lived in Myanmar, I realize my perspective is necessarily limitedbut sometimes outsider observations can be useful. What I've found is that Myanmar faces a unique set of challenges and opportunities that differ significantly from other Asian languages' modernization experiences. The country's deep Buddhist philosophical traditions and complex writing system create both obstacles and genuine advantages. While technical issues like Unicode support remain frustrating, Myanmar's cultural wisdom-particularly around mindfulness, ethical reasoning, and community cooperation-seems increasingly relevant to global academic discussions. I've looked at how Japan, Korea, and Finland have handled language modernization, trying to extract useful lessons. What emerges is something I'm calling a "culture-driven technological adaptation" approach, though I'm sure Myanmar scholars will find plenty to criticize in my analysis. The key insight, I think, is that Myanmar's international value doesn't lie in becoming another generic "international language" but in offering genuinely distinctive conceptual frameworks to global knowledge systems.

title: Judicial Pillars for Sale: The Irony of the Umbrella Chain

detail.title: Judicial Pillars for Sale: The Irony of the Umbrella Chain
detail.abstract: This article takes the "umbrella chain(San-chain)" as the core concept to reveal the implicit shielding structure formed by the interconnection of political achievements, the judiciary, chambers of commerce, and gray industries in local governance. First, the article analyzes the composition of the umbrella chain, showing how it forms a smooth shielding network through publicity, political-legal departments, courts, public security, chambers of commerce, and gray industries. Second, it dissects the operational logic of the umbrella chain, presenting a progressive shielding script from "shielding first when encountering problems" to "shifting blame to the extreme". Then, within the Field-Shi framework, it clarifies how the fields of political achievements, the judiciary, chambers of commerce, and culture provide legitimacy and potential energy for the umbrella chain. The article further uses the SBFFE framework to explain the five-fold cycle of the umbrella chain, analyzes the "smoothing out" of ordinary criminal cases and the "extreme operations" of tampering with judgments, and reveals the different risk levels of the two types of umbrella chains through the comparison between the Black-umbrella chain and the White-Shell umbrella (business front) chain. Finally, the article points out that the ultimate fate of the umbrella chain lies in collapse: once the evidence overflows and the fields become ineffective, the SBFFE cycle breaks layer by layer, and the umbrella chain changes from smooth operation to a void state. As a reflection, this article positions the umbrella chain as a value trap, which forms a mirror image contrast with the logic of the cutter: the former brings short-term benefits but long-term destruction, while the latter leads to short-term quietness but long-term tranquility. In summary, the umbrella chain is not only a real slice of local governance but also the best sample of institutional fragility.

detail.abstract: Regulators and other governors rely on intermediaries to set and implement policies and to regulate targets. Existing literatures focus heavily on intermediaries of a single type-Opportunists, motivated solely by self-interest. But intermediaries can also be motivated by different types of loyalty: to leaders (Vassals), to policies (Zealots), or to institutions (Mandarins). While all three types of loyalists are resistant to the traditional problems of opportunism (slacking and capture), each brings pathologies of its own. We explain the behavioral logic of each type of loyalty and analyze the risks and rewards of different intermediary loyaltiesboth for governors and for the public interest. We illustrate our claims with examples drawn from many different realms of regulation and governance.

detail.abstract:
This paper specifies the Newro protocol, a novel economic and monetary system designed for an era in which artificial intelligence (AI) is a primary agent of production. 

The protocol introduces the Newro (NWR), a currency the issuance of which is intrinsically and verifiably linked to the creation of valuable cognitive output by AI. The core of the system is the Five Layer Value Confirmation Protocol (FLVCP), a technical mechanism that quantifies and validates claims of value creation through five distinct, measurable stages: Data, Cognition, Outcome, Verification, and Backing. 

Newro's monetary model is founded on the principle of "Proof of Useful Work," where every computation that secures the system also contributes to a valuable economic or scientific outcome. The currency is anchored by a treasury of productive real-world assets, including compute and energy, which provides a defensible value floor. To ensure the equitable distribution of AI-driven productivity gains, the protocol integrates a Universal Basic Income (UBI) for all verified citizens. 

Governance is managed through a bicameral system, balancing the interests of token holders with the broader community of unique human participants. This document provides a complete specification for the FLVCP, the Newro tokenomic model, the system's architecture, and its governance framework, with the objective of establishing a transparent, stable, and equitable economic foundation for a flourishing economy driven by artificial cognition.

title: Enhancing Fiscal Stability through Medium-Term Tax Strategies and Inflation-Adaptive Policies

detail.title: Enhancing Fiscal Stability through Medium-Term Tax Strategies and Inflation-Adaptive Policies
detail.abstract: Amid persistent macroeconomic volatility and inflationary pressures, international financial institutions have increasingly underscored the importance of fiscal consolidation as a cornerstone for sustainable public finance. Central to this objective is the adoption of mediumterm budgetary frameworks (MTBFs) featuring medium-term revenue strategies (MTRSs), which promote a coordinated, multi-year approach to tax reform that integrates policy design, administration, and legal structures. This paper examines the efficacy of medium-term tax plans, targeting the excisable goods market (e.g., alcohol, sugar-sweetened beverages, tobacco, fuel), by constructing a theoretical model comparing government revenue outcomes under a six-year rule-based plan with steady annual rate increases, against alternative biennial and triennial ad hoc tax adjustment scenarios. Furthermore, the analysis considers the revenue implications of indexation mechanisms (i.e., the automatic adjustment of tax rates to a select inflationary benchmark). Findings indicate that formal multi-year tax plans with scheduled annual increases markedly improve revenue stability and accumulation compared to ad hoc revisions. While indexation remains a useful mechanism for preserving the real value of revenues, it does not facilitate real revenue growth, underscoring the necessity for a dual strategy: utilizing indexation as a baseline safeguard to maintain the real value of revenues in inflationary settings, combined with formal multi-year tax plans. This dual policy allows governments to achieve real revenue growth, enhancing fiscal stability.

title: Machines are more productive than humans until they aren’t, and vice versa

detail.title: Machines are more productive than humans until they aren’t, and vice versa
detail.abstract: With the growth of artificial skills, organizations are increasingly confronting the problem of optimizing skill policy decisions guided by economic principles. This paper addresses the underlying complexity of this challenge by developing an in-silico framework based on Monte Carlo simulations grounded in empirical realism to analyze the economic impact of human and machine skills, individually or jointly deployed, in the execution of tasks presenting varying levels of complexity. Our results provide quantitative support for the established notions that automation tends to be the most economically-effective strategy for tasks characterized by low-to-medium generalization difficulty, while automation may struggle to match the economic utility of human skills in more complex scenarios. Critically, our simulations highlight that, when a high level of generalization is required and the cost of errors is high, combining human and machine skills can be the most effective strategy, but only if genuine augmentation is achieved. In contrast, when failing to realize this synergy, the human-machine policy is severely penalized by the inherent costs of its dual skill structure, causing it to destroy value and become the worst choice from an economic perspective. The takeaway for decision-makers is unambiguous: in complex and critical contexts, simply allocating human and machine skills to a task may be insufficient, and a human-machine skill policy is neither a silver-bullet solution nor a low-risk compromise. Rather, it is a critical opportunity to boost competitiveness that demands a strong organizational commitment to enabling augmentation. Also, our findings show that improving the cost-effectiveness of machine skills over time, while useful, does not replace the fundamental need to focus on achieving augmentation.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces a novel combined bootstrap methodology for the analysis of stationary long-memory time series, addressing the challenges posed by their persistent dependence structures. Unlike existing hybrid approaches that merge algorithms at the procedural level, our method combines independently generated bootstrap samples from a variety of established techniques, including parametric, semi-parametric, and block-based methods, into a unified composite sample. This integration is performed using both simple (mean, median, trimmed mean) and performance-based (correlation, MSE, MAE, regression-based) combination schemes. Through extensive Monte Carlo simulations and empirical applications to the Nile River minima and Microsoft stock returns, we show that the combined bootstrap approach yields improved estimation accuracy for the long-memory parameter d, particularly in terms of root mean squared deviation and confidence interval coverage. The proposed method is shown to mitigate model misspecification risk and improve inference robustness. While our focus is on estimating the long-memory parameter, the approach is general and can be extended to other statistics and dependence structures. This work offers a new perspective on bootstrap methodology and opens avenues for future theoretical and practical advancements.

title: Five Years After Rana Plaza: The Way Forward

detail.title: Five Years After Rana Plaza: The Way Forward
detail.abstract:
The collapse of the Rana Plaza factory complex in Bangladesh in April 2013 killed 1,134 people and refocused attention on working conditions in the global garment industry. This report marking the fifth anniversary examines the forces that contributed to the disaster, the response since 2013, and what needs to happen in the future. One of the questions we raise is whether Bangladesh offers lessons for protecting human rights in international supply chains. We conclude that to a degree it does, but more work needs to be done to make the country’s export factories safe.


In the wake of Rana Plaza, major clothing brands and retailers formed two unusual initiatives in Bangladesh. Hennes & Mauritz (H&M), Primark, and other European companies joined with trade union partners to create the Accord on Fire and Building Safety in Bangladesh. Walmart, Gap, and other North American companies set up the Alliance for Bangladesh Worker Safety. While there are important differences between these two initiatives, both did factory inspections and oversaw remediation. Accord and Alliance members agreed to cease all business with Bangladeshi manufacturers that declined to comply.


As we explain in Part Two, the foreign initiatives have improved conditions in many factories. They are not, however, panaceas. Today they cover only about 2,300 active factories serving their member companies. The Bangladeshi government separately retains oversight for another 1,650 or so. But this still leaves out a very large number of additional factories—and their workers. 


Many of the left-out factories primarily do subcontracting work for export, or a combination of production for the local and global markets, and thus do not have direct relationships with the large Western buyers. Subcontractors play a crucial role, helping larger “mother” factories manage their export workload.

detail.abstract: Inflation is the measure of price increase of a basket of essential items for everyday living. Hence, inflation goes up and down depending on demand and supply of essential items, and critically on whether there are technological improvements in the essential items. Thus, is there a baseline level of inflation that can be attributed to technological improvements? Here, I propose a new metric called, Technological Price Index (TPI), to better reflect how technological improvements can drive up prices of essential items. To account for technological improvements, it is important to use a more fine-grained approach at analysing the technological level of an essential item. Take, for example, a laptop, a technological improvement can be moving from WiFi 5 to WiFi 6, or from Bluetooth 5.1 to Bluetooth 5.2. Another example would be moving from conventional rice to genetically engineered rice. Hence, the price increase can be accounted for by tracking the changes in technological level of products, which can be a proxy for baseline inflation level. Note here that as a technology matures, and is mass produced and widely adopted, its price becomes cheaper. Thus, the Technological Price Index will similarly move up and down to track the emergence of new technology, and its gradual widespread adoption.

detail.abstract: Early childhood care and education (ECCE) constitute an essential basis for children's comprehensive development and lifelong learning and, considered a vital strategy for attaining equitable and sustainable development. India, being one of the most populous nations with a significant young demographic, lacks substantial evidence for thorough research on transition of the ECCE system and comparative analysis in light of imported commercialisation of education and digitalisation. To address these gaps in the literature and get a pragmatic understanding of India's position, we conduct a hybrid thematic analysis guided by Theory of human capital and Heckman's theory of the significance of earlylife investment. The results indicate that evolution of Indian ECCE system embodies a choice between persistent indigenous pedagogical ideologies and external Western paradigms. India has developed a policy framework aimed at equality, inclusion, and quality through integrated, child-centred, play-based methodologies yet enduring inequalities in access, quality, and educational achievements continue to be crucial challenges, that can hinder the achievement of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 4.2 by 2030. Findings also indicate that India's ECCE trajectory parallels that of fellow emerging nations. The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) position India as a regional leader in intent; however, the realisation of universal, high-quality, equitable ECCE necessitates the integration of global best practices such as nationwide adoption of play-based, culturally relevant, and inclusive pedagogy, emphasis on bridging between public-private entities.

title: Redefining the Risk Quotient: A Generalized Framework for Fragility Analysis Across Study Designs

detail.abstract: The Risk Quotient was introduced to normalize the Relative Risk Index, offering an interpretable alternative to fragility metrics tied to P values. However, the initial formulation defined the Risk Quotient as the Relative Risk Index divided by the total sample size, limiting interpretability and comparability. We propose a unified definition: the Relative Risk Index is the average absolute residual between the observed table and the neutrality table (expected counts under therapeutic neutrality), and the Risk Quotient is the Relative Risk Index normalized by the average cell count. This definition yields a Risk Quotient ranging from 0 (perfect neutrality) to 1 (maximum possible deviation), which makes it directly interpretable as the minimum percent of outcomes that must change to eliminate any observed treatment effect. We demonstrate its extension from 2×2 tables to contingency tables of any size, including continuous outcomes reframed as contingency tables. This refinement standardizes the Risk Quotient across study types, resolves definitional conflicts, and enables a common interpretive framework for evidence robustness.

title: Fragility of the Fragility Index: When Calculation Becomes Impossible

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No competing interests declared.

detail.abstract: Background: The Fragility Index (FI) may become unattainable under Fisher's exact test constraints in common clinical trial scenarios, including rare events, balanced small samples, and extreme imbalances. Methods: We analyzed 14 representative 2×2 tables spanning rare events, balanced designs, and extreme imbalances, and computed alternative fragility metrics. Results: FI was not attainable in all 14 cases. Risk Quotient (RQ), Percent Fragility Index (PFI), and Relative Risk Index (RRI) computed in 14/14; Robustness Index (RI) in 12/14. Conclusions: FI is not attainable in everyday scenarios. Robust fragility metrics include the RQ, which quantifies distance to therapeutic neutrality on a bounded 0-1 scale, and the PFI, which quantifies the percentage change needed to flip statistical significance.

detail.abstract: Deciding on the timing and stringency of pandemic mitigation represents a critical challenge for healthcare operations management. Key objectives for policymakers include safeguarding the healthcare system by ensuring reliable access to ICUs for patients, while simultaneously limiting mitigation measures to avoid overburdening society. These goals are pursued under uncertainty in the illness’s transmission rate. We propose a stochastic optimization framework that addresses these objectives and accounts for the transmission uncertainty. We capture the pandemic dynamics through a compartmental epidemic model with susceptible-exposed-infectious-recovered-died compartments, and we apply the developed framework to real COVID-19 data from four Nordic countries. Our findings contribute to the public discourse on mitigation timing and stringency by showing that it may be optimal to delay the onset of mitigation (as observed for Denmark, Finland, and Sweden) or to alternate between strict and lenient measures (as in Norway), depending on a country’s ICU capacity, prevailing pandemic conditions, and policy objectives. Furthermore, our results demonstrate that optimal mitigation strategies can achieve a 95% reliability target for ICU access while requiring, on average, approximately 40% fewer ICUs than the actual strategies implemented. This research responds to Anderson et al. (2023)’s call for evaluating the impacts of different national COVID-19 mitigation policies. This study also addresses a gap in nonconvex polynomial chance-constrained problems and proposes a new second-order cone formulation for the envelope of bilinear terms.

title: Still Struggling: Migrant Construction Workers In Qatar During The Pandemic
affiliations: New York University (NYU) - New York University

detail.title: Still Struggling: Migrant Construction Workers In Qatar During The Pandemic
detail.abstract:
Qatar has relied on hundreds of thousands of migrant workers from South Asia to build the stadiums, highways, and other infrastructure needed for the 2022 World Cup soccer tournament, which the Arabian Gulf emirate will host in November. In addition to the historic hardships facing migrant laborers in the Middle East, Qatar’s foreign workforce has been hit hard by the Covid-19 pandemic, beginning in early 2020. 

This report uses Qatar as a case study to examine how the global public health crisis affected destitute migrants in the Middle East and how employers and the government responded. It also makes a series of reform recommendations that would promote human rights by improving workers’ economic and living conditions. 

The report’s central findings are twofold: After a slow start, the government of Qatar provided migrant workers with free, adequate healthcare in response to the pandemic. But foreign laborers suffered economically as a result of construction delays, wage reductions, terminated contracts, and deportations. The contrast between the government’s vigorous public health campaign and its failure to protect workers’ livelihoods is key. Qatar should address migrants’ economic needs with the same energy and resourcefulness illustrated by its efforts to stem the spread of Covid-19. 

The handling of recruitment fees provides an example of how migrant workers in Qatar and the rest of the Middle East continue to be economically exploited. International labor law requires that employers cover costs associated with the recruitment and transportation of foreign workers. Qatari law is more ambiguous, however. In general, it prohibits charging migrant workers for their own recruitment but doesn’t specify that employers should cover these costs. Under special worker-welfare standards established for World Cup stadium projects, construction companies are supposed to pay for recruitment. And key arms of the government that hire such companies have pledged to ensure that the contractors fulfill this responsibility. As a result, the percentage of foreign workers helping to build World Cup stadiums who have paid for their own recruitment has diminished over the last several years, according to surveys funded by the government.

detail.abstract: Between 2023 and 2025, cyber-enabled financial crimes reached unprecedented levels, combining cryptocurrency thefts, banking breaches, and hybrid laundering networks into a complex global ecosystem of digital exploitation. This paper analyzes empirical data from FATF, Chainalysis, TRM Labs, INTERPOL, IMF, and FinCEN to reveal a ten-billion-dollar convergence of financial cybercrime and transnational terrorism financing. It further evaluates institutional countermeasures, highlighting structural weaknesses in regulatory coordination. Finally, it introduces the s.id framework—a privacy-preserving, compliance-by-design digital-identity architecture that operationalizes global AML/CFT principles through verifiable credentials, AI-driven risk scoring, and zero-knowledge proofs.

title: Accounting Classification Entropy
affiliations: University of Minnesota - Twin Cities - Carlson School of Management, Tepper School of Business, Carnegie Mellon University, Carnegie Mellon University - David A. Tepper School of Business and

detail.title: Accounting Classification Entropy
detail.abstract: We theoretically develop and empirically apply a new information measure that quantifies the structural dimension of financial statements. Building on the entropy concept from Shannon's (1948) information theory, our approach captures firm fundamentals directly embedded in accounting numbers and formally measures the information conveyed by their classification structure. The measure is transparent, easy to implement, and adaptable across various classification-based settings. Using balance sheet data for U.S. public firms, we construct firm-quarter entropy-based measures and examine their relationship with market-based proxies that indirectly capture information content. In the first extension, we further demonstrate the measure's empirical usefulness by applying it to explain financial analysts' attention allocation decisions. In the second extension, we illustrate the framework's flexibility by incorporating richer accounting structures using the concept of mutual information and exploring additional empirical applications. Overall, our study offers a theory-based yet practical measure of financial statement classification that complements existing approaches to quantifying accounting information.

title: The Reputation-Equilibrium Paradox (REP Theory): A Dynamic Model of Self-Destroying Efficiency
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Reputation-Equilibrium Paradox (REP Theory): A Dynamic Model of Self-Destroying Efficiency
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Reputation-Equilibrium Paradox (REP Theory), which explains how decision-making based on collective reputation leads to cyclical inefficiencies in economics, trade, and policy. Unlike classical Nash Equilibrium, where strategies stabilize, REP Theory demonstrates that reputational equilibria are self-destroying: the very act of collective convergence undermines the efficiency of the reputed option. Applications range from traffic flows and financial markets to trade routes and policymaking, offering insights into how adaptive strategies can outperform reputation-driven herding.

title: Gaming The System: How Extremists Exploit Gaming Sites And What Can Be Done To Counter Them
affiliations: University of Chicago - Law School

detail.title: Gaming The System: How Extremists Exploit Gaming Sites And What Can Be Done To Counter Them
detail.abstract:
Extremist actors are exploiting online gaming sites to disseminate violent ideologies, network with likeminded people, and perpetrate real-world harm. The sites where these actors operate include both those offering online video games and “gaming-adjacent” platforms, which host content and discussions related to gaming. 

This report draws on existing literature; fresh interviews with gamers, gaming company executives, and experts; and findings from a multinational survey of gamers conducted in January 2023. 

Online gaming is an enormous industry unto itself. In 2022, the global video game industry generated revenue of almost $200 billion and provided entertainment to more than three billion consumers around the world. The largest technology companies—including Microsoft, Amazon, Apple, Facebook, and Google—are heavily invested in gaming as owners of major game studios and their blockbuster titles, dominant distribution platforms, and popular gaming-adjacent sites. 

A growing body of evidence shows that bad actors exploit basic features of video games and adjacent platforms to channel hate-based rhetoric, network with potential sympathizers, and mobilize for action—sometimes with deadly consequences. The relative ease with which extremists have been able to manipulate gaming spaces points to the need for urgent action by industry actors to avoid further harm. Although some gaming companies have made recent investments in content moderation technologies and systems, most companies are still far behind in terms of adequately governing and mitigating abuse of their platforms.

This call to address extremist exploitation became more urgent in April 2023 in the wake of media reports that the large gaming-adjacent platform, Discord, had been used by a young U.S. air national guardsman for the reckless and allegedly illegal sharing of top-secret military documents, which then were spread to other online sites. Separately, Microsoft's president, Brad Smith, revealed in an interview in April that his company had detected Russian operatives seeking to infiltrate discussion groups on Discord made up of people who play Microsoft's popular online game Minecraft.

title: Junior Golf: Examining the Economic Reality of Seeking a Scholarship

detail.title: Junior Golf: Examining the Economic Reality of Seeking a Scholarship
detail.abstract: Junior golf represents one of the most financially demanding youth sports in America, with families often investing between $150,000 and $300,000 over a 13-year period. Yet the potential return—college golf scholarships—is limited and unevenly distributed: only 13.2% of top-ranked boys and 51.0% of top-ranked girls receive any Division I or II athletic aid. This study investigates whether junior golf functions as a viable financial investment or an expensive gamble, drawing on national data, scholarship statistics, and personal case studies. Through detailed cost breakdowns, comparative scholarship analysis, and peer investment profiles, this research reveals a significant economic mismatch between money spent and money earned through college funding. While the vast majority of junior golfers will never recoup their investment, this paper argues that financial return should not be the primary justification for participation. Instead, the real value of junior golf lies in the development of life skills, character, and networking opportunities that extend far beyond scholarship dollars. Ultimately, junior golf offers meaningful long-term benefits—but not necessarily financial ones—making honest expectation setting essential for families navigating this costly pursuit.

title: Understanding Customer Perception of Luxury Fashion Through Online Comunnities and Blogs
affiliations: Kyungsung University and Kyungsung University

detail.title: Understanding Customer Perception of Luxury Fashion Through Online Comunnities and Blogs
detail.abstract: Luxury fashion is gaining popularity globally due to the internet and online blogs. Companies need to understand the perception of luxury fashion customers to succeed in marketing. The definition of luxury has evolved and is constantly changing. Luxury has historical ties to religion and societal status. Today, social media and technology play a significant role in shaping the luxury fashion industry, with brands engaging younger consumers online. The study aims to understand the ideas shared among online luxury fashion customers by analyzing commonly used words through big data tools. Limitations include the use of a localized search engine and the exclusion of certain countries such as China. Future research could improve accuracy by analyzing data from major search engines worldwide.

title: Beyond the Deal: Towards Equity in Music
